title: Lost Money to Online Fraud in India? What to Do and Whom to Report To
html:
If money has just left your account because of a fraud, do these in order and fast. Call your bank and block the card or UPI. Report it on the national cybercrime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in. Tell your bank about the transaction in writing and keep the proof. RBI's rules on customer liability depend on how quickly you report to the bank.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Rules change. Where this page quotes a rule, the source is linked, and your bank's own staff have the final word on your case.

Sources last checked: 10 Oct 2026.

1. Call your bank now

Use the number printed on your card or inside your bank's official app, not a number from a message or a search result. Ask them to block the card, UPI or net banking, and to note the time you reported the problem. Reporting quickly matters: see the RBI rule below.

2. Report to the cybercrime helpline or portal

Sanchar Saathi, the Department of Telecommunications portal, says that if you have already lost money you should report it to the cybercrime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in. On the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, choose Register a Complaint and pick Financial Fraud if money was taken. The portal also has a Report Suspect facility where you can report identifiers such as websites, phone numbers, email addresses and social media links.

3. Tell your bank in writing, and know the RBI rule

Send your bank an email, or use its complaint form or app, so that you have the time of your report. RBI's circular of 6 July 2017 on limiting customer liability in unauthorised electronic banking transactions says:

  • If the loss was due to a breach elsewhere in the system and you tell the bank within three working days of the bank's message about the transaction, you have zero liability.
  • If you report in four to seven working days, your liability is limited to the transaction value or a capped amount in the circular's table, whichever is lower.
  • The bank must credit the disputed amount to your account within 10 working days of your notice, and settle the complaint within 90 days.
  • You are expected to register for SMS alerts and to report at the earliest.

That circular is about unauthorised transactions and is from 2017. Whether it covers a payment you were tricked into making yourself, and whether a newer RBI rule applies to you, is for your bank to answer. Ask the question in writing and keep the reply.

4. Keep the proof

  • Screenshots of the messages, call log, payment screen and any website or app involved.
  • Transaction ID or UTR, amount, date and time, and the account or UPI ID that received the money.
  • The phone numbers, email addresses and links used by the person who contacted you.
  • The complaint number you get from the portal or helpline, and your bank's reference number.

5. Report the number or message on Chakshu

On Sanchar Saathi, Chakshu lets you report suspected fraud communication by call, SMS or WhatsApp, for example messages about KYC updates, your bank account, SIM, gas or electricity, someone impersonating a government official, or sextortion. The portal says to report within 30 days. Chakshu is for preventing more fraud; it is not where you report lost money.

The blocking and reporting steps on your phone are in our spam call guide.

6. Secure your accounts

If you shared a password, an OTP or a UPI PIN, change it now and sign out of other devices. Our guides for your Google account and checking your phone list the steps. Never share an OTP with a caller: see what an unrequested OTP means.

What to do next

  1. Call your bank on the official number and block the card or UPI.
  2. Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in, and save the complaint number.
  3. Write to your bank, and note the date and time.
  4. Report the number or message on Chakshu within 30 days.
  5. Change passwords and sign out of unknown devices.
